ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The Iron Ox of Shaanfu is a named object in a recurring case, while other iron-ox passages use the durable animal figure without naming that monument.
EvidenceBody: The Shaanfu Iron Ox is the corpus's fixed place-named iron ox, distinct from an unplaced iron-ox figure. Chan masters make it an impossible moving stage-object and public answer. Fenyang Shanzhao answers a question about the student's turning place by saying to water the Shaanfu Iron Ox. Linxi Wenqing's hall address pairs it with the great image of Jiading and makes the two cross their named regions: the image comes through the pass while the Iron Ox enters western Shu. Baiyu Si says that a fire beneath Lake Tai frightens it into running to Silla. These place-name, pairing, watering, and travel predicates establish the recurring named object, but the stored witnesses do not establish what physical object it was or whether it was cast.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: This separate corpus sense names iron-ox figure, not the Shaanfu Iron Ox. The stored cases keep that referent explicit.
EvidenceBody: An iron-ox figure is an unplaced ox image that Chan masters put into comparisons, mechanism language, and impossible actions. Yaoshan Weiyan compares his former position at Shitou Xiqian to a mosquito on an iron ox. Guishan Lingyou sharpens the physical scene: a mosquito on the iron ox has nowhere to put its mouth. Fengxue Yanzhao compares the patriarchal mind-seal to the mechanism of an iron ox and stages a public exchange over whether to apply the seal. Zhenjing Kewen has a hornless iron ox break an iron barrier, and Yandang Wenji places one in a lineage answer beside the barren woman who bears a child. Baichi Yuan's verse directly speaks of casting an iron ox, establishing a cast object in that occurrence without making casting part of every use. Hongzhi Zhengjue says one tug by the iron ox snaps a gold rope. These are deployments of the generic figure, not the specifically named Shaanfu Iron Ox.
